system.summary: Two-part numerical code of four-digit groups (all seen between 1000 and 1749), written with commas between groups. Mainly a syllabary of letters and syllables (1020 de, 1267 la, 1501 s, 1232 tion) with code words for names and terms (1217 Russie, 1532 Suede, 1104 Grand Vizir, 1280 l'Empereur, 1584 traite, 1684 alliance). u and v are one element. Rebuilt in part: 85 confirmed values.
system.notes: Homophones: several groups give the same letter or syllable (s = 1501, 1601, 1075, 1557; le = 1655, 1656). The order of the groups is not alphabetical as far as seen. The margin tags 1440 and 1529 mark the speakers A and B of a written-out dialogue and were never glossed. The 18 mixed values may be loose glosses or homophones not yet separated. No nulls identified.

prior_solution.where: The contemporary decipherment written over the groups on images 255-257 and 260 (and other glossed pages of the volume). No edition or modern decipherment found (one web search, 3 Nov 2026). S. Kuneralp's edition of Villeneuve's reports from Constantinople (ISIS Press, vol. 4, 1736-1739) mentions approaches by Höpken and Carlson; it is not a decipherment and was not opened.

solution.what: Images 255-266 and 320-328 of R0003582 fetched from the Riksarkivet IIIF service, one at a time, 1.2 s apart.
Target repository checked for claims on Höpken, Carlson or R0003582; one web search for an edition or decipherment.
Glossed runs of images 255-257 transcribed in two passes (pass 2 blind, digits only); disagreements settled on crops.
Hard-EM segmentation of each run against the French written over it, from 74 seed values read by eye. Key from 255-257 frozen (sha256 in FROZEN.sha256) before image 260 was transcribed.
Held-out image 260 (14 runs, 164 groups), frozen key: 111 groups decode to exactly the gloss letters at their place; 500 shuffled keys: mean 25.5, maximum 36.
Final key from all pairs plus 9 hand-set code words; readings written as the contemporary French with every place the key does not give marked in place; scripts/check_marks.py passes.
Bare postscript on image 263 (55 groups) decoded with the final key.

Independent check (VERIFY.md): blind transcription of all 164 groups of 260, 2 raw disagreements, 0 confirmed solver errors, 1 unresolved; byte-identical rebuild; held-out test reproduced; verdict 'fix'.

Fixes applied: ten word-crossing EM values demoted (key_demoted.tsv); 1532 = Suede aligned in 260 h04; 1601? marked; postscript note corrected; word counter now counts each gloss word inside a multi-word mark; readings regenerated, check_marks passes.

outcome.method_basis: The glossed runs are transcriptions of the 18th-century decipherment written over the numbers. The rebuilt code list gives 59% of their words from confirmed values and was tested on a held-out page; it reads nothing the gloss does not already give.

texts.label: Enclosure of 2/13 Dec. 1739: a reported conversation, speakers A and B (images 255-257)
texts.summary: A written-out dialogue between A (the Swedish side) and B, very probably the French ambassador Villeneuve, mediator of the Belgrade peace: B denies that the peace with Russia was his work and says the peace with the Emperor was concluded without Russia being stipulated; the two discuss the Porte, the Grand Vizier and a Swedish-Ottoman defensive alliance.
texts.note: A transcription of the contemporary decipherment, confirmed in part by the rebuilt code list; not a break. 234 words: 143 (61%) from confirmed key values, 41 (18%) on single or mixed values, 50 (21%) on the gloss alone. read_share = the confirmed share. B = Villeneuve is a proposal from content only.

reading_review.by: AI language-model agent (for WAINUT; a model reading, not a person), independent of the solver
reading_review.note: The French reads coherently because it is the contemporary gloss; the English is faithful. Weak places: 256 r13 (5 marks); 256 r15 (8 marks, 'aux instances', 'du ... Sultan meme', with 1221 'du' marked as having no counterpart); 256 r16 (blot, 'flegme' rests on the gloss alone); 257 r47 (1260 que against 'stipule', 'fait'); 255 r05 (blank in the gloss); 255 r07 ('Cour, ni'). The identification B = Villeneuve rests on content only, and the file says so. [Graded before the clean-up of 3 Nov 2026: the word-crossing EM values named here were then demoted out of the key, and the words they carried now count as resting on the gloss.]

texts.note: A transcription of the contemporary decipherment. 14 words: 5 (36%) from confirmed key values, 2 (14%) on single or mixed values, 7 (50%) on the gloss alone.

texts.label: Conversation report of 1740, image 260 left page (the held-out passage)
texts.summary: Speaker A argues that the Porte ministers' fear that Russia would no longer keep the stipulated conditions if the Porte made a defensive treaty with Sweden is unworthy of so great an empire; any petty prince may form an innocent friendship for mutual security, and if Russia took offence she would show her designs on her neighbours.
texts.note: Held-out result, frozen key: 111 of 164 groups match the independent gloss (68% of all, 80% of known); 500 shuffled keys: mean 25.5, maximum 36. The word counts use the final key, which was trained on this page too, so they are NOT held-out figures: 68 words, 38 (56%) confirmed, 6 (9%) single or mixed, 24 (35%) gloss alone.

reading_review.by: AI language-model agent (for WAINUT; a model reading, not a person), independent of the solver
reading_review.note: Coherent, with a good translation. Weak places: in h04, 'Suede est' is carried by the artefact 1481 = 'suedeest' while the code word 1532 is marked as having no counterpart, and 'fait' rests on the gloss; h09 'amitie' uses 1474 = 'damit'; h11 'ombrage' is counted through 1573 = 'itombra'; h12 'mauvaises desseins' and h13 'intentions' are mostly gloss. The counts come from a key trained on this same page. [Graded before the clean-up of 3 Nov 2026: the word-crossing EM values named here were then demoted out of the key, and the words they carried now count as resting on the gloss.] h04 now aligns 1532 = Suede.
